title: OT Connector Sample Envelope
description: A single read result published to te/device/<device>/ot/<protocol>/sample/<point>. A sample is a time series row: identity, value, quality. Everything static per point — the unit, the labels, the access, the free-form meta table and the device's type — is published once on the device manifest (§8.2) instead of on every read.

ts.description: Read completion time, RFC 3339, millisecond precision, UTC (Z). A consumer needing epoch milliseconds parses it (there is no second timestamp field).

protocol.description: The protocol module that produced the sample — a fact about its origin, and what ot-measurement groups by.

datatype.description: The point's datatype (§4) — always present, because it is the only type system: 'bytes' is the raw case, whose value is the hex of what was read. With the JSON type of 'value' it carries everything the removed 'value_repr' said, and it tells a consumer that a string-typed 'value' is an int64 outside the JSON safe range (§4.1).

value.description: The point's value: the decoded primitive, or — for datatype 'bytes' — the hex of what was read. Absent when quality=bad.

error.description: Human-readable failure reason. Required when quality=bad.

raw.description: Hex of the bytes read, words space-separated in protocol-natural width. Present only under [connector] sample_debug (§3.3): a debugging aid, not part of the default envelope.

addr.description: Protocol-specific address echo; shape defined by each connector spec. Present only under [connector] sample_debug (§3.3): the address is static per point and the manifest's job.

examples.error: modbus exception: gateway target device failed to respond
